body:
Upstream issue: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/35270

Mirror issue: https://github.com/amdpilot-org/sglang/issues/1401

## What changed

A dLLM unresolved denoise block is rewritten in place, so its token IDs are not stable enough for the radix tree to own. The prior unfinished-request path cached that page; on the next denoise step a different key could claim the same physical KV page, inflating evictable accounting and failing the idle pool invariant.

This change adds a request accessor that excludes only `dllm_incomplete_ids` and uses it in the classic and unified radix-cache unfinished paths. Once the block resolves, the full committed prefix remains cacheable.

## Reproduction and verification

The regression uses real CPU paged pools and the actual cache implementations. Before the source fix, the classic cache accounted 128 tokens while its nodes referenced only 96 tokens of distinct physical pages. After the fix, classic and unified ownership checks pass, along with resolved-block and short-request boundary cases.

```
/tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-d58e7286dc7e/venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_dllm_volatile_radix_block.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_radix_cache_unit.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_decode_radix_lock_ref.py
# 54 passed, 61 subtests passed
```

The assigned accelerator was confirmed as gfx950 / AMD Instinct MI350X, and a Torch GPU reduction matched its CPU reference. That is hardware-execution evidence only, not a full-model reproduction.

## Limitations

LLaDA2.1 weights and Ascend hardware were unavailable, so I did not rerun the original 256-request HTTP workload. SWA, Mamba, and experimental C++ radix caches were not exercised with dLLM and are intentionally outside this narrow change. No native code changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.

Detailed claims and retained evidence paths are in `reports/j-d58e7286dc7e/result.json`.
